:::{#thm-density-limit}
#### A density as a limit of interval probabilities

If $X$ is a continuous random variable with density $f$,
and $f$ is continuous at $x$,
then $f(x)$ is the limit of the probability that $X$ falls in an interval starting at $x$,
divided by the width of that interval,
as that width shrinks to 0:

$$f(x) = \lim_{\change \downarrow 0} \frac{\Pr(x \le X < x + \change)}{\change}$$

:::

::: proof

For $\change > 0$:

$$
\ba
\frac{\Pr(x \le X < x + \change)}{\change}
&= \frac{\Pr(x < X \le x + \change)}{\change}
&& \text{(} \Pr(X = x) = 0 \text{ and } \Pr(X = x + \change) = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \frac{\cdff{x + \change} - \cdff{x}}{\change}
&& \text{(additivity, and the definition of the CDF)}
\ea
$$

By @thm-cdf-derivative-is-density, $\cdf$ is differentiable at $x$ with $\cdf'(x) = f(x)$,
so this difference quotient converges to $f(x)$ as $\change \downarrow 0$.

:::
